Direction – Social Democracy: Slovakia. The party identifies as social-democratic, and was described as a combination of "leftist economics and nationalist appeal".

Songhai Empire: Songhay. The Songhai Empire was a state located in the western part of the Sahel during the 15th and 16th centuries.

Western Roman Empire: Latin. The Western Empire collapsed in 476, and the Western imperial court in Ravenna disappeared by 554, at the end of Justinian's Gothic War.
Of which country was Washington-on-the-Brazos the capital?

Washington-on-the-Brazos is the capital of Republic of Texas. The Republic of Texas (Spanish: República de Tejas), or simply Texas, was a short-lived sovereign country in North America from March 2, 1836, to February 19, 1846.

Named in the opening chapters of Genesis, this figure is considered the first human aware of God across several Abrahamic faiths, and in Christian tradition, his sin in Eden introduced death into the world — who is he?
Adam is the name given in Genesis 1-5 to the first human.
The daughter of an Imperial Russian general, she served as People's Commissar for Welfare and became the first woman in history to sit in a national cabinet — who was this Bolshevik?
Alexandra Kollontai was Soviet politician and diplomat (1872–1952).
Once co-leader of Alliance 90/The Greens alongside Robert Habeck, she became Germany's foreign minister and then president of the UN General Assembly's 80th session — who is she?
Annalena Baerbock (born 15 December 1980) is a German diplomat and politician of the Alliance 90/The Greens party.
This 9th-century Iranian revolutionary's uprising was considered an offshoot of neo-Mazdakism and showed the enduring strength of pre-Islamic Persian identity in the region — who led it?

Babak Khorramdin (795 or 798 - January 838) was one of the main Iranian revolutionary leaders of the Iranian Khorram-Dinn ("Those of the joyous religion"), which was a local freedom movement fighting the Abbasid Caliphate.
Which former campaign manager for Hillary Clinton represented Brooklyn on the City Council before being elected mayor of New York City in 2013?
Bill de Blasio (born Warren Wilhelm Jr., May 8, 1961) is an American former politician who served as the 110th mayor of New York City from 2014 to 2021.
Having founded Turkey's first bank, İş Bankası, this politician went on to become prime minister under Atatürk and later the country's president throughout the 1950s — who is he?
Celâl Bayar (16 May 1883 - 22 August 1986) was a Turkish economist and politician who was the president of Turkey from 1950 to 1960.

This 8th-century Byzantine emperor exploited civil war in the Muslim world to press the Arab frontier, then resettled Christians in Thrace to tighten his grip on the Balkans against the Bulgars — who was he?
Constantine V (July 718 - 14 September 775) was Byzantine emperor from 741 to 775.
An American politician and businessman who served as the 46th vice president under George W. Bush from 2001 to 2009, considered the architect of the Iraq War—who was he?
Dick Cheney (January 30, 1941 - November 3, 2025) was an American politician and businessman who served as the 46th vice president of the United States under President George W. Bush.
A daughter of Peter the Great, she ruled from 1741 to 1762 and stayed beloved partly for a remarkable vow: not to execute a single person during her reign — which empress?
Elizabeth of Russia was Empress of Russia (1741–1762). During her reign Elizabeth continued the policies of her father and brought about a remarkable Age of Enlightenment in Russia.
The CEO of the ACS engineering group, this Spanish businessman is better known as the football boss who launched the 'Galácticos' policy of signing the world's best players — who is he?
Florentino Pérez (Spanish; born 8 March 1947) is a Spanish businessman and the president of football club Real Madrid, as well as chairman and CEO of ACS Group, a civil engineering company.
This Roman general and politician, adopted by his uncle Tiberius in AD 4, is best remembered for his campaigns against the German chieftain Arminius. Who was he?
Germanicus (24 May 15 BC - 10 October AD 19) was a Roman general and politician most famously known for his campaigns against Arminius in Germania.
Ascending the throne in 2020 after his cousin's death, this monarch became the fifteenth ruler of a dynasty that has led Oman since the 18th century — who is he?
Haitham bin Tariq (born 11 October 1955) is the Sultan and Prime Minister of Oman.

Colonial history of the United States

Democratic Front for the Liberation of Palestine

Indian Rebellion of 1857 was a major uprising in India in 1857-58 against the rule of the British East India Company, which functioned as a sovereign power, including military forces, on behalf of the British Crown.
In the Book of Genesis, this son of Noah appears in the story of Noah's drunkenness and is later named ancestor of the peoples of the Aegean, Anatolia, and Greece — who is he?
Japheth was one of the three sons of Noah in the Book of Genesis.
This U.S. president assumed office in 1841 after his predecessor died just 31 days into his term, becoming the first vice president ever to ascend to the presidency this way — who is he?
John Tyler (March 29, 1790 - January 18, 1862) was the tenth president of the United States, serving from 1841 to 1845, after briefly holding office as the tenth vice president in 1841.
A former Director of Public Prosecutions, this Labour leader became the UK's Prime Minister in 2024 — who is he?
Keir Starmer (born 2 September 1962) is a British politician and former lawyer who has served as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom since 2024 and as Leader of the Labour Party since 2020.
In Christian eschatology, this future event will see Jesus Christ return to sit on a "great white throne" and render a final verdict on every person who has ever lived — what is this event called?
Last Judgment is a central Christian eschatological event marking the return of Jesus Christ to evaluate all of humanity, both the living and the resurrected dead (Jn 5:28-29).

He fought in the Burma Campaign for the British Indian Army and retired a Pakistani colonel, then in 1971 became commander-in-chief and founder of a brand-new nation's armed forces — which four-star general was he?
M. A. G. Osmani (1 September 1918 - 16 February 1984) was a Bangladeshi military officer, revolutionary and politician.
Developed in the Soviet Union by Joseph Stalin, this communist ideology became the predominant state ideology across the Eastern Bloc during the Cold War. What is it?
Marxism–Leninism is a communist ideology that became the largest faction of the communist movement following the October Revolution.
Twice shot in the head and surviving both times, this Russian field marshal later defeated Napoleon's invasion using a strategy of attrition — who was he?
Mikhail Kutuzov was Field Marshal of the Russian Empire (1745–1813).
France's longest-serving head of state across 22 years, he was the country's second president and its very last monarch, deposed in 1870 — who was he?
Napoleon III (born Charles-Louis Napolon Bonaparte; 20 April 1808 - 9 January 1873) was President of France from 1848 to 1852 and then Emperor of the French from 1852 until his deposition in 1870.
Often shown as a nude woman covered in stars and arching protectively over the Earth, this Egyptian deity embodies the sky itself — who is she?
Nut (goddess) (Ancient), also known by various other transcriptions, is the goddess of the sky, stars, cosmos, mothers, astronomy, and the universe in the ancient Egyptian religion.
He started out as a care officer for Camden Council before his drag character Lily Savage made him a household name on British television — which performer was he?
Paul O'Grady (14 June 1955 - 28 March 2023) was an English drag queen, comedian, broadcaster, actor, and writer.
Established by Hitler on 16 March 1939, the day after German troops occupied the Czech rump state, this partially annexed Nazi territory was home mostly to ethnic Czechs — what was it called?
Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia was a partially annexed territory of Nazi Germany that was established on 16 March 1939 after the German occupation of the Czech lands.
Founder of the System Capital Management investment group, this billionaire is both Ukraine's richest man and the owner of football club Shakhtar Donetsk — who is he?
Rinat Akhmetov (born 21 September 1966) is a Ukrainian oligarch, billionaire and businessman.

A hero of the Texas Revolution, this statesman served as both the first and third president of the Republic of Texas, and is the only American ever elected governor of two different states. Who was he?
Sam Houston (March 2, 1793 - July 26, 1863) was an American military general and statesman who played a prominent role in the Texas Revolution.
This Indian politician has served two separate terms as Chief Minister of Karnataka, and was only the second person ever to complete a full five-year term in that office — who is he?

Siddaramaiah (born 3 August 1947), also referred to by his nickname Siddu, is an Indian politician, lawyer, former lecturer and statesman who served as the 16th Chief Minister of Karnataka from 2013 to 2018 and 2023 to 2026.
Before becoming French prime minister in 2025, this Renaissance party politician held ministerial posts covering local authorities, overseas territories, and the armed forces — who is he?
Sébastien Lecornu (French; born 11 June 1986) is a French politician who has served as Prime Minister of France since September 2025.

Recognized only by the Soviet Union and Mongolia, this partially-recognized socialist state in North Asia existed for 23 years before its parliament requested absorption into the Russian SFSR in 1944 — what was it, whose territory now forms a namesake region of Russia?
Tuvan People's Republic (TPR), known simply as Tuva, was a partially recognized socialist republic that existed between 1921 and 1944 in North Asia.

This German Generalfeldmarschall (1891–1945) began as a hard-driving panzer commander but became known as a practitioner of defensive warfare. He gained Hitler's attention early and commanded the Ninth Army in 1941–1942 — who is he?
Walter Model (24 January 1891 - 21 April 1945) was a German Generalfeldmarschall during World War II.

Founded in London in 1844 by George Williams, this now-global youth organization serves over 64 million people across 120 countries and promotes healthy body, mind, and spirit development — name the organization?
YMCA is a worldwide youth organization based in Vernier, Canton of Geneva, Switzerland, with more than 64 million beneficiaries in 120 countries.
A grandson of caliph Abu Bakr and the first child born to Islam's earliest converts, he led a rival caliphate based in Mecca during the Second Fitna until his death in 692 — who was he?
Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr: Arab leader of Mecca-based caliphate from 683 to 692.

Founded in British India in the late 19th century by Mirza Ghulam Ahmad, who claimed to be the promised Messiah and Mahdi awaited by Muslims, this messianic movement is centered on his teachings — name the movement?

Ahmadiyya: Islamic messianic movement founded by Mirza Ghulam Ahmad. Adherents of the Ahmadiyya—a term adopted expressly in reference to Muhammad's alternative name Ahmad—are known as Ahmadi Muslims or simply Ahmadis.
Tutored by Aristotle, this Macedonian king succeeded his father at age 20 and by age 30 had conquered an empire stretching from Greece to northwestern India, undefeated in battle — who was he?
Alexander the Great: King of Macedon from 336 to 323 BC.
As a key figure in Boris Yeltsin's government, this economist oversaw Russia's post-Soviet privatization before fleeing to Israel in 2022 — who is he?
Anatoly Chubais: Russian politician and economist (born 1955)
After her weaving skills provoked the wrath of Minerva in Ovid's telling, this mortal hanged herself in shame and was transformed into a spider -- who is she?
Arachne: Mythological weaver who was transformed into a spider.

Born in Somalia and granted asylum in the Netherlands at 23, this writer and activist entered Dutch centre-right politics after renouncing her childhood faith and identifying as an atheist — who is she?
Ayaan Hirsi Ali: Somali-born activist, politician, and author (born 1969)
Fought twice over the same New York ground in the fall of 1777, this Revolutionary War clash ended with a British army's surrender and persuaded France to join the American cause — what is it?
Battles of Saratoga: Part of the American Revolutionary War. The second battle ended with a decisive American victory, and the surrender of the British army there.

With six engines slung in nacelles beneath its swept wings — a design borrowed from captured German research — this Cold War-era American bomber was built to outrun Soviet interceptors at high altitude — which aircraft?
Boeing B-47 Stratojet: Cold War-era American jet bomber. The primary mission of the B-47 was as a nuclear bomber capable of striking targets within the Soviet Union.
This Italian-born prelate succeeded Richelieu as chief minister to the French crown in 1642, guiding young King Louis XIV's early education — who is he?
Cardinal Mazarin: Italian clergyman and politician (1602–1661)
Nicknamed 'the Rash,' this last great Duke of Burgundy dreamed of carving out an independent kingdom stretching from the North Sea to Savoy, clashing with his overlord King Louis XI. Who was he?
Charles the Bold: Duke of Burgundy from 1467 to 1477.

Beginning in 1964 and rooted in a period of violence sparked by the 1948 assassination of a liberal leader, this decades-long struggle pitted the government against far-right paramilitaries and far-left guerrillas like the FARC — what's it called?
Colombian conflict: Low-intensity asymmetric war in Colombia.

While working at the RAND Corporation, this analyst leaked the top-secret Pentagon Papers to The New York Times in 1971, facing a 115-year maximum sentence before charges were dismissed over illegal evidence-gathering — who is he?
According to Virgil's Aeneid, which mythical queen fled her tyrannical brother as joint ruler of Tyre to found the city of Carthage in what's now Tunisia?
Dido: Legendary founder and first queen of Carthage.
Nicknamed 'Toby,' this barrister summed up his dream as 'a nation for a continent, and a continent for a nation' and became Australia's very first prime minister in 1901 — who is he?
Edmund Barton: Prime Minister of Australia from 1901 to 1903.
Formed in 1204 in the Pontus region with backing from Georgia's Queen Tamar, this Byzantine successor state endured on Anatolia's northeastern coast into the 15th century — which realm?
Empire of Trebizond: Byzantine rump state (1204–1461)

After warning that hidden conspirators and calumniators surrounded him, without naming names, a French revolutionary leader was arrested the next day and executed by guillotine on 28 July 1794, paving the way toward more moderate policies — which event is this?
Fall of Maximilien Robespierre: 1794 event during the French Revolution.

A teenage Bosnian Serb student in Sarajevo, his two pistol shots on 28 June 1914 killed an archduke and his wife — and set off the July Crisis that led to World War I. Who was he?
Gavrilo Princip: Assassin of Archduke Franz Ferdinand (1894–1918)
Spanning from 37 BC to 668 AD, this kingdom sprawled across the northern Korean peninsula and into Manchuria, and its name literally means 'high castle' — which realm was it?
Goguryeo: Korean kingdom (c. 37 BC–668 AD). Along with Paekche and Silla, Goguryeo was one of the Three Kingdoms of Korea.
According to Genesis, this Egyptian woman bore Abraham's firstborn son, Ishmael, and though unnamed in the Quran, Islam regards her as his second wife — who is she?
This period of Japanese history spanned the entire reign of Emperor Akihito, beginning the day after his father's death in January 1989 and ending with his abdication in 2019 — what was it called?
Heisei era: Period of Japanese history (1989–2019). Thus, 1989 corresponds to Shōwa 64 up until 7 January and Heisei 1 (平成元年, Heisei gannen; gannen means "first year") from 8 January.

This German banker headed the Reichsbank in both the Weimar Republic and the early Nazi era, and helped persuade Hindenburg to appoint Hitler's first government despite later opposing some rearmament policies — who is he?
Hjalmar Schacht: German politician, banker, and economist (1877–1970)
Dictating an account titled 'A Gift to Those Who Contemplate the Wonders of Cities,' this 14th-century Tangier-born traveler covered roughly 117,000 km — more than Marco Polo or Zheng He — who is he?
Ibn Battuta: Maghrebi traveller and scholar (1304–1368/1369)

Inheriting leadership of a Sufi military order from his brother as a child, this ruler founded a Persian dynasty in 1501 and unified Iran under native rule for the first time in over eight centuries. Who was he?
Ismail I: Shah of Safavid Iran from 1501 to 1524.
Representing Maryland's 8th congressional district since 2017, this progressive Democrat also founded Democracy Summer, a nationwide youth civic-organizing program — who is he?
A scholar and lawyer who inherited the Trujillo era's secretive, caudillo style, he served three non-consecutive terms as president of the Dominican Republic between 1960 and 1996 — who was he?
Joaquín Balaguer: President of the Dominican Republic (1960–1961, 1966–1978, 1986–1996)
Born in Georgia and rising as a Soviet revolutionary, this figure led from 1924 to 1953 while consolidating power into a dictatorship and codifying Marxism–Leninism — who was he?
Joseph Stalin: Leader of the Soviet Union from 1924 to 1953.
A German naval officer who once commanded U-boat UB-68 in WWI, he briefly became Nazi Germany's head of state after Hitler's suicide in April 1945 — who is it?

Ruled for most of its existence by Regent Miklos Horthy despite having no actual monarch on the throne, this interwar Central European state emerged after the suppression of a short-lived Soviet republic during the White Terror — which nation?
Kingdom of Hungary (1920–1946): Monarchy under regency.
An ethnic Georgian who rose through the Cheka and became head of the NKVD in 1938, this secret police chief organized the Katyn massacre and ended his predecessor Yezhov's purge — who is he?
Lavrentiy Beria: Soviet secret police chief (1899–1953)
Affectionately nicknamed 'Nessie,' this long-necked cryptid supposedly lurking in a Scottish Highlands lake shot to worldwide fame in 1933 — what is it?
Loch Ness Monster: Mythical creature in Scottish folklore.
Elected in 2020, this North Carolina congressman became the first member of Congress born in the 1990s, before controversies helped end his reelection bid in 2022 — who is he?
Twice queen consort of England through her marriage to Henry the Sixth, this daughter of the King of Naples personally led the Lancastrian side during the Wars of the Roses — who is she?
Margaret of Anjou: Queen of England (1445–1461, 1470–1471)
A brigadier general who led El Salvador through most of World War II, he served as the country's 27th president until resigning in 1944 — which Salvadoran officer?
Maximiliano Hernández Martínez: President of El Salvador from 1931 to 1934 and 1935 to 1944.
Plucked from running Russia's Federal Taxation Service, this economist was confirmed as prime minister in a single day in January 2020 after the entire previous government resigned — who is it?
Mikhail Mishustin: Russian politician and economist (born 1966)
Hidden by his mother among the bulrushes of the Nile as a baby, this prophet grew up to lead the Israelites out of slavery in Egypt. Who is he?
More than just nudism, this lifestyle and movement frames non-sexual social nudity around harmony with nature and respect for the environment — what is it called?
Naturism: Practice and advocacy of social nudity.

Sparked by a 1962 coup that toppled a newly crowned king and proclaimed a republic — and even abolished slavery — this conflict pitted royalists backed near the Saudi border against the new government. Which war was it?
North Yemen civil war: 1962–1970 conflict. The war began with a coup d'état carried out in 1962 by revolutionary republicans led by the army under the command of Abdullah al-Sallal.
Hebrew for 'Jewish Power,' this far-right Israeli political party grew out of the banned Kach movement and was linked in its early years to politician Itamar Ben-Gvir — which party?
Otzma Yehudit: Israeli far-right political party. Otzma ran independently in the 2013 election and as part of a list with ultra-Orthodox party Yachad in 2015.
Based on the doctrine of a 20th-century Argentine leader, this political movement is defined by three 'flags' — social justice, economic independence, and political sovereignty — what is it called?
Peronism: Argentine political movement. Peronism, also known as justicialism, is an Argentine ideology and political movement, based on the ideas, doctrine, and legacy of Juan Perón (1895–1974).
This act of deliberate communication with a deity — through hymns, incantations, or spontaneous words — has been documented in written sources for some five thousand years — what is it called?
Prayer: Invocation or act that seeks to activate a rapport with a deity.
Ascending the Siamese throne in 1782 following the deposition of King Taksin, this monarch became the first ruler of the Chakri dynasty and founded the city that is now Bangkok — who was he?
Rama I: King of Siam from 1782 to 1809.
A Labour politician who served two decades on the Kensington and Chelsea council, she also worked as a senior lecturer at Kingston University — who is she?
Rima Horton: English former councillor and economics lecturer (born 1947)
Beginning in February 2014 with Russia's annexation of Crimea and a war in the Donbas, this conflict escalated into Europe's biggest war since World War II — what is it called?
Russo-Ukrainian war: Ongoing conflict since 2014. It then supported Russian separatist armed groups who started a war in the eastern Donbas region against Ukraine's military.
Married for more than 40 years to a celebrated general, this English courtier's close bond with Queen Anne made her one of the most powerful women in early 18th-century Britain — who was she?
Sarah Churchill, Duchess of Marlborough: English noblewoman, courtier and politician (1660–1744)
Growing out of the 19th-century Millerite movement and formally founded in 1863, this denomination observes Saturday as the Sabbath and reveres the writings of co-founder Ellen G. White — what is it?
The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
Seventh-day Adventist Church: Protestant Christian denomination.
After finishing third in Turkey's 2023 presidential race, this far-right politician became a so-called kingmaker by throwing his support behind Erdoğan — who is he?
A former professor turned politician, this leader has served in India's upper house of parliament since 2019 and acts as a senior national spokesperson for the Bharatiya Janata Party — who is he?
Prince Arthur, Duke of Connaught and Strathearn
Younger brother of a U.S. president and an attorney general, he represented Massachusetts in the Senate from 1962 until his death in 2009 — which long-serving senator?
Ted Kennedy: American lawyer and politician (1932–2009)
This retired Royal Navy vice admiral served as an equerry to Queen Elizabeth II before marrying her only daughter in 1992 — who is he?
Timothy Laurence: Retired Royal Navy officer (born 1955)
This nontrinitarian Christian movement rejects the traditional three-in-one God concept, instead viewing Jesus Christ as a supreme moral teacher subordinate to a singular Creator — what is it?
The illegitimate son of Mircea I of Wallachia, this nobleman was inducted into the Order of the Dragon in 1431 and twice ruled Wallachia as Voivode in the 1430s and 1440s — who is he?
Vlad II Dracul: Ruler of Wallachia (r. 1436–1442, 1443–1447)
Introduced to the public in 1954 by a retired British civil servant, this modern pagan, Earth-focused religion blends ancient motifs with 20th-century hermetic ideas — which religion?
Wicca: Modern syncretic pagan religion. Wicca draws upon ancient pagan and 20th-century hermetic motifs for theological and ritual purposes.

After his father — a former Andhra Pradesh chief minister — died in a 2009 helicopter crash, this politician toured the state on a consoling 'Odarpu Yatra' before founding his own party and later becoming chief minister himself — who is he?

Y. S. Jagan Mohan Reddy: Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh, India. Jagan Mohan Reddy started his political career in the Indian National Congress and was elected as the Member of Parliament of Kadapa in 2009.
This ancient Iranian faith centers on the Avesta and reveres Ahura Mazda as the supreme, uncreated deity, teaching a struggle between Asha (truth) and Druj (the lie). What religion is it?
Zoroastrianism: Iranian religion founded by Zoroaster.

Oliver Heaviside (born 1850) is the earliest of the four. Although at odds with the scientific establishment for most of his life, Heaviside changed the face of telecommunications, mathematics, and science.
Which of these four is the eldest?
Henrietta Swan Leavitt (born 1868) is the earliest of the four. Henrietta Swan Leavitt (July 4, 1868 – December 12, 1921) was an American astronomer.
Which of these four came first?
C++ (founded 1983) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four was released earliest?
Pascal (programming language) (published 1972) is the earliest of the four.
Pick the mathematician from these four.
Jim Simons is a mathematician. James Harris Simons (April 25, 1938 – May 10, 2024) was an American hedge fund manager, investor, mathematician, and philanthropist.
What is the atomic number of Ruthenium?
Ruthenium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ru and atomic number 44.
What is the atomic number of Chlorine?
Chlorine is a chemical element; it has symbol Cl and atomic number 17.
In what year was Marie Curie born?
Marie Curie: Curie was born in Warsaw, Russian Empire, where she studied at the clandestine Flying University and began her practical scientific training.
In what year was Nitroglycerin discovered?
Nitroglycerin: It is combined with nitrocellulose to form double-based smokeless powder, used as a propellant in artillery and firearms since the 1880s.
In what year was Thallium discovered?
Thallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Tl and atomic number 81.
Ceftriaxone: Pfizer. Ceftriaxone, sold under the brand name Rocephin, is a third-generation cephalosporin antibiotic used for the treatment of a number of bacterial infections.
In which country is Convair B-58 Hustler based?
Convair B-58 Hustler: United States. The Convair B-58 Hustler is a supersonic strategic bomber, the first capable of Mach 2 flight.
Who is credited with discovering Dubnium?
Dubnium: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research. Dubnium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Db and atomic number 105.
Who is credited with discovering Brainfuck?
Brainfuck: Urban Müller. Brainfuck is an esoteric programming language created in 1993 by Swiss student Urban Müller.
Who is credited with discovering Cobalt?
Cobalt: Georg Brandt. Cobalt is a chemical element; it has symbol Co and atomic number 27.
Home to both edible and poisonous species, this fungal genus supplies the West's most popular cultivated mushrooms, including the everyday button mushroom — which genus is it?
Agaricus is a genus of mushroom-forming fungi containing both edible and poisonous species, with over 400 members worldwide and possibly again as many disputed or newly discovered species.
Found on every continent but Antarctica and almost always monogamous breeders, which bird family unites ducks, geese, and swans under one scientific name?
Anatidae are the biological family of water birds that includes ducks, geese, and swans.
Native to Europe and Asia, which genus of burdock plants owes its seed-dispersal success to burrs that later inspired a famous fastening invention?
Arctium is a genus of biennial plants commonly known as burdock, family Asteraceae.
Created in 1989 by Brian Fox for the GNU Project as a free replacement for the Bourne shell, this command-line interpreter became the default login shell on countless Linux systems — which shell?
Bash (Unix shell) (short for "Bourne Again SHell") is an interactive command interpreter and command language developed for Unix-like operating systems.
Native to India and Nepal, this medium-sized antelope sports a striking two-tone coat, with males growing corkscrew horns up to 75 cm long. Which animal is it?
Blackbuck (Antilope cervicapra), also known as the Indian antelope, is a medium-sized antelope native to India and Nepal.
This small leafy vegetable, a cultivar of cabbage grown for its edible buds, shares its name with a European capital — what is it?
Brussels sprout is a member of the Gemmifera cultivar group of cabbages (Brassica oleracea), grown for its edible buds.

This American astronomer and planetary scientist was initially an assistant professor at Harvard before moving to Cornell as the David Duncan Professor of Astronomy. He played an active role in the Voyager programs. Who is he?
Carl Sagan (November 9, 1934 - December 20, 1996) was an American astronomer, planetary scientist and science communicator.
Patented in 1948 and used to treat hay fever and other allergic conditions, this first-generation antihistamine works within two hours by blocking the H1 histamine receptor — name the drug?
Chlorphenamine (CP, CPM), also known as chlorpheniramine, is an antihistamine used to treat the symptoms of allergic conditions such as allergic rhinitis (hay fever).

This highly venomous, nocturnal snake, black or bluish-black with narrow white crossbands, is widely distributed across South Asia, from grasslands to agricultural fields to human settlements — what snake is it?
Common krait (Bungarus caeruleus) is a highly venomous snake species belonging to the genus Bungarus in the family Elapidae.
Its name comes from the Greek for "dark blue," and its anion — a carbon triple-bonded to nitrogen — is so toxic that salts like the sodium and potassium forms cause swift poisoning. What is it?
Cyanide (from Greek kyanos 'dark blue') is an inorganic chemical compound that contains a CN functional group.
This Russian chemist's great law let him predict three undiscovered elements — germanium, gallium, and scandium — and a synthetic element now bears his name; who was he?
This Russian economist served as Vladimir Putin's economic adviser before becoming governor of her country's central bank, and was ranked among Forbes' most powerful women in 2019 — who is she?
Elvira Nabiullina (born 29 October 1963) is a Russian economist and current governor of the Central Bank of Russia.
This sensory organ detects light and converts it into electro-chemical signals in neurons, using an adjustable lens system to focus incoming light and form images — name the organ?
Eye is a sensory organ that allows an organism to perceive visual information.
He worked on uranium enrichment during the Manhattan Project, then — after McCarthyism cost him his physics post — founded San Francisco's hands-on Exploratorium museum; who was he?

Frank Oppenheimer (August 14, 1912 - February 3, 1985) was an American particle physicist, cattle rancher, professor of physics at the University of Colorado, and the founder of the Exploratorium in San Francisco.
The largest and outermost of the three hip muscles, this one shapes the buttocks and helps keep the human trunk upright — what muscle is it?
Gluteus maximus is the main extensor muscle of the hip in humans.
Though usually grouped with the birch family, some botanists split this deciduous shrub genus into its own family — and its nut is a popular snack — which plant?
Hazel are plants of the genus Corylus of deciduous trees and large shrubs native to the temperate Northern Hemisphere.
Named for a Greek youth beloved by Apollo and slain by a jealous wind god who then transformed him into this fragrant spring bloom — what flower genus is it?
Hyacinth is a genus of bulbous herbs and spring-blooming perennials.
Resembling a lump of burnt charcoal growing on birch bark, this parasitic fungus is popularly called chaga — what's its scientific name?
Inonotus obliquus (a Latinization of the Russian word), is a fungus in the family Hymenochaetaceae.
Holder of 128 firearm patents, this American engineer invented the telescoping bolt that made compact autoloading pistols possible — who is he?

John Browning (January 23, 1855 - November 26, 1926) was an American firearm designer who developed many varieties of military and civilian firearms, cartridges, and gun mechanisms, many of which are still in use around the world.
Despite its name suggesting a root vegetable, this biennial cultivar of wild cabbage grows a swollen edible stem above ground and is related to broccoli, kale, and Brussels sprouts — what is it?
Kohlrabi (scientific name Brassica oleracea Gongylodes Group), also called German turnip or turnip cabbage, is a biennial vegetable, a low, stout cultivar of wild cabbage.

Named after the Italian word for lemon, this colorless liquid hydrocarbon is the main compound behind citrus peel fragrance, occurring mostly as a right-handed form extracted commercially by centrifugal separation or steam distillation - name the compound?

Limonene is a colorless liquid aliphatic hydrocarbon classified as a cyclic monoterpene, and is the major component in the fragrance and essential oil of citrus fruit peels, taking its name from Italian limone ("lemon").
This marsupial family native to Australia and New Guinea includes kangaroos, wallabies, quokkas, and tree-kangaroos among its 63 living species — what family is it?
Macropodidae is a family of marsupials that includes kangaroos, wallabies, tree-kangaroos, wallaroos, pademelons, the quokka, and several other groups.
This nitrogen-heavy compound forms durable plastic resins used in dry-erase boards and dinnerware, and its foam version scrubs stains as the innards of a Magic Eraser — name the chemical?
Melamine is an organic compound with the formula C3H6N6.
This SI base unit for amount of substance, symbol mol, is defined so that one unit contains exactly 6.02214076×10²³ elementary entities — what is it called?
Mole (unit) (symbol mol) is a unit of measurement, the base unit in the International System of Units (SI) for amount of substance.

The first recognized fossil of this archaic human group was unearthed in 1856 in a German valley, and the species vanished around 40,000 years ago as modern humans arrived; who were these Pleistocene Europeans?

Neanderthal (nee-(r)-TAHL, nay-, -THAHL; Homo neanderthalensis or sometimes Homo sapiens neanderthalensis) are an extinct group of archaic humans who inhabited Europe and Western and Central Asia during the Middle to Late Pleistocene.

Synthesized in 2002 at a lab near Moscow and named in 2016 for the physicist who hunted down the heaviest atoms, this synthetic element claims the highest atomic number and atomic mass of anything yet known — which is it?
Oganesson is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Og and atomic number 118.
Found in organs such as the brain and lungs, inside flatworms, and within leaf cross-sections, this word names an organism's bulk functional tissue — what is it?
Parenchyma is the bulk of functional substance in an animal organ such as the brain or lungs, or a structure such as a tumour.
Made in the body from the amino acid L-phenylalanine, this natural stimulant also turns up in fermented chocolate and inhibits a transporter called VMAT2 — what is it?
Phenethylamine (PEA) is an organic compound, natural monoamine alkaloid, and trace amine, which acts as a central nervous system stimulant in humans.
It looks like a single point of light, but this brightest star of Ursa Minor is actually a triple star system parked near the north celestial pole — what is it?
Polaris is a yellow supergiant star in the northern circumpolar constellation of Ursa Minor.
This noncontagious autoimmune condition leaves dry, scaly patches of skin and can flare at the exact spot of an injury — a quirk called the Koebner phenomenon; what is it?
Psoriasis is a long-lasting, noncontagious autoimmune disease characterized by patches of abnormal skin.

This condition, often triggered by crush injuries or extreme exercise, causes skeletal muscle to break down so rapidly that it can turn urine tea-colored and damage the kidneys — what condition is it?
Rhabdomyolysis (shortened as rhabdo) is a condition in which damaged skeletal muscle breaks down rapidly.
Contracted from contaminated food, this bacterial illness typically causes diarrhea, fever, and cramps within a day or two of exposure — what is it called?
Salmonellosis is a symptomatic infection caused by bacteria of the genus Salmonella.
Cartilaginous and toothy, these fish are the sister group to the rays and skates and trace their ancestors to the Devonian Period — what are they?

Shark are a group of elasmobranch cartilaginous fishes characterized by a ribless endoskeleton, dermal denticles, five to seven gill slits on each side, and pectoral fins that are not fused to the head.
This leafy green vegetable's high oxalate content gives raw and cooked versions noticeably different flavors, with blanching helping to tone it down — what vegetable is it?
Spinach (Spinacia oleracea) is a leafy green flowering plant native to Central and Western Asia.
This South African biologist established the tiny roundworm C. elegans as a model organism, work that helped earn him a share of the 2002 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. Who was he?
Sydney Brenner (13 January 1927 - 5 April 2019) was a South African biologist.

Beloved by biologists for its wild morphological variation and elaborate nest-building, this northern fish tolerates big swings in salinity, living in the sea but breeding in fresh water — what is it?
Three-spined stickleback (Gasterosteus aculeatus) is a fish native to most inland and coastal waters north of 30N.
These large, heavyset American game birds have a distinctive fleshy growth called a snood hanging from the base of their beak, with wild and ocellated species. What birds are they?
Turkey (bird) are large, heavyset galliforms in the genus Meleagris, indigenous to the Americas.
This pungent Japanese condiment, ground from the rhizome of a plant related to horseradish and mustard, traditionally accompanies sushi. What is it?

This teenage prodigy's work on solvable polynomials helped birth what's now called group theory, and his fiery Republican politics landed him in prison before a fatal duel ended his life at 20 — who was he?
Évariste Galois (25 October 1811 - 31 May 1832) was a French mathematician and political activist.
This practice leans on 'branding' — tying a name or image to certain qualities in people's minds — to nudge them toward buying more. What field is it?
Advertising: Form of communication for marketing.
This German polar researcher proposed in 1912 that the continents were slowly drifting apart, a theory mainstream geology only accepted decades later thanks to palaeomagnetism — who was he?
Alfred Wegener: German climatologist and geophysicist (1880–1930)
Critically endangered with barely two dozen wild individuals estimated in 2007, this big cat subspecies survives along the Russian-Chinese border in the Primorye region — which spotted predator?
Amur leopard: Subspecies of large cat. The Amur leopard (Panthera pardus orientalis) is a leopard subspecies native to the Primorye region of southeastern Russia and northern China.
This external body opening at the end of the digestive tract, positioned opposite the mouth, lets gas and solid waste pass out after digestion?
Anus: Digestive tract waste expulsion opening. Passage of feces through the anus is typically controlled by muscular sphincters, and failure to stop unwanted passages results in fecal incontinence.
Native to Eurasia, this perennial plant is grown as a vegetable crop for its tender young shoots, harvested in the spring — what's this vegetable?
Asparagus: Species of flowering plant in the family Asparagaceae.

Once the go-to sedatives and anticonvulsants, these barbituric-acid-derived depressants were largely replaced by benzodiazepines and 'Z-drugs' because of their high addiction and overdose risk — what class of drugs?
Barbiturate: Class of depressant drugs derived from barbituric acid.
This English musician played bass on the Rolling Stones' first nineteen studio albums across three decades before later fronting his own blues outfit, the Rhythm Kings — who is he?
Developed from a wide-body airliner and selected in 2011 to replace an aging fleet of aerial tankers, this refueling aircraft entered US Air Force service in 2019 — which aircraft?
Boeing KC-46 Pegasus: American military aerial refueling and transport aircraft.
Native to Australia and naturally green and yellow with black scalloped markings, this small, long-tailed parrot is one of the world's most popular pet birds — what is it?
Encompassing wolves, dogs, coyotes, and golden jackals, which genus is defined by its members' massive skulls, long legs, and comparatively short ears and tails?
Canis: Genus of canines. Canis is a genus of the Caninae which includes multiple extant species, such as wolves, dogs, coyotes, and golden jackals.
This mint-family herb, described by Carl Linnaeus in 1753, takes its common name from its long historical association with cats — which plant?
Catnip: Nepeta cataria; species of plant.

One of the earliest cultivated legumes — its oldest traces were unearthed in Syria — this protein-packed seed goes by names like garbanzo and chana, and forms the backbone of hummus and falafel. What is it?
Chickpea: Species of flowering plant with edible seeds.
Sold as Catapres and Kapvay, this drug treats high blood pressure, ADHD, and drug-withdrawal symptoms, and can be delivered via a skin patch — what is it?
Renowned for a gift of mimicry noted by Pliny the Elder and Shakespeare, this glossy black bird has a bill that turns from black in winter to yellow in summer — what species is it?
Common starling: Species of passerine birds.
Surprisingly, the closest living relatives of birds are a clan of semiaquatic predators that includes alligators, caimans, and the long-snouted gharial. What is this reptile order?
Crocodilia: Order of reptiles. The teeth are conical and peg-like, and the bite is powerful.
This Manhattan Project physicist later led the Federation of American Scientists and is best remembered for his 1959 Senate testimony opposing Lewis Strauss's Commerce nomination — who is he?
David L. Hill: American nuclear physicist (1919–2008)
Named for the unique double-beamed bones under its tail, this long-necked Jurassic giant is one of the most common fossils found in North America's Morrison Formation. What dinosaur is it?
Diplodocus: Genus of diplodocid sauropod dinosaurs (fossil)
Starting life bilaterally symmetrical as larvae but growing into five-pointed radial adults, this animal phylum includes starfish, sea urchins, and sea cucumbers — what is it called?
Echinoderm: Marine phylum of animals often with radial symmetries.
This branch of zoology, whose name derives from Greek words for 'insect' and 'study,' covers a field that has described over 1.3 million species — which discipline?
The only Old World member of its family to breed in the Northern Hemisphere's temperate zones, this migratory songbird winters in central and southern Africa — what is it?
Eurasian golden oriole: Species of bird.
This Swiss thinker, alongside Charles Sanders Peirce, is considered one of the two founders of semiotics — the field he himself called 'semiology' — who is he?
Ferdinand de Saussure: Swiss linguist and philosopher (1857–1913)
Marked by physical traits such as a long face, large ears, and unusually flexible fingers, this inherited neurodevelopmental disorder stems from a repeat expansion in the FMR1 gene — which condition?
Fragile X syndrome: X-linked dominant genetic disorder.
This is the largest lizard family, boasting over 950 species that cling to surfaces via Van der Waals forces in their toe hairs — including house, tokay, and day varieties — which family?
Gekkonidae: Family of lizards. Gekkonidae (the common geckos) is the largest family of geckos, containing over 950 described species in 62 genera.
Caused by iodine deficiency in over 90% of cases worldwide, this neck swelling results from an enlarged thyroid gland — what's the condition called?
Goitre: Neck swelling due to enlarged thyroid gland. A goitre (British English, spelled goiter in American English) is a swelling in the neck resulting from an enlarged thyroid gland.

This French civil engineer made his name building railway bridges like the Garabit Viaduct and later helped erect the Statue of Liberty, before retiring to study meteorology and aerodynamics — who was he?
This Dutch-born entrepreneur produced Japan's first major turn-based role-playing game and later secured the console distribution rights to a Russian puzzle game called Tetris — who is he?
Henk Rogers: Dutch-born American computer programmer (born 1953)
Despite the name, this 'living fossil' is no crustacean at all — it's a chelicerate, kin to spiders and scorpions, and its three-part body ends in a spiky tail called a telson. What creature is it?
Horseshoe crab: Family of basal chelicerates.
This physical phenomenon describes how a system's current state depends on its past history, forming looping curves in magnets and giving hard disk drives their memory — what is it?
Hysteresis: Dependence of the state of a system on its history. Hysteresis can be found in physics, chemistry, engineering, biology, and economics.
An English polymath who was also an alchemist and theologian, he shares credit with Leibniz for inventing calculus and wrote the Principia — who is he?
As chief engineer, this man designed the Mitsubishi A6M Zero, Japan's iconic World War II fighter plane, and later worked on the postwar NAMC YS-11 airliner — who is he?

Caused by a herpesvirus and linked to weakened immunity such as HIV/AIDS, this cancer produces purple skin lesions and disproportionately affects older Mediterranean men in its 'classic' form — which condition?
Kaposi's sarcoma: Cancer of the skin, integumentary lymph nodes, or other organs.
This reddish-brown, bitter tincture dissolved opium poppy extract in alcohol and was once sold without a prescription as a cough and pain remedy — what is it?
Laudanum: Tincture of opium. Laudanum is a tincture of opium containing approximately 10% powdered opium by weight (the equivalent of 1% morphine).
This soft, movable pair of appendages on the jaw helps with eating and speech, and is often used in kissing — what are they?
Lip: Visible body parts at the mouth.
The sole member of its genus in the soapberry family, this sweet, mildly tart fruit carries a distinctive rose-like aroma and comes in Indochinese, Philippine, and Javanese subspecies — what is it?
Boiled down from its sap to make a beloved breakfast syrup, this genus of roughly 132 tree and shrub species counts the sycamore as its type species — which genus of trees?
Made up of the dura, arachnoid, and pia mater, these three protective membranes shield the brain and spinal cord while containing cerebrospinal fluid — what are they called?
Meninges: Three membranes protecting the brain. In anatomy, the meninges (sing. meninx; from Ancient Greek μῆνινξ (mêninx) 'membrane') are protective membranes that cover the brain and spinal cord.

Soviet pilots called it the "Balalaika" because its planform looked like the stringed instrument, while Poles dubbed it "Ołówek" — the pencil — for its slender fuselage; which most-produced supersonic jet in history earned all those nicknames?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-21: 1956 Soviet fighter aircraft family.
Native to northern India, this fast-growing, drought-resistant tree is nicknamed the 'drumstick tree' for its seed pods and the 'horseradish tree' for its pungent roots — what is it?
Moringa oleifera: Species of flowering tree.
Made of two fused benzene rings, this pungent white crystalline compound is the main ingredient in traditional mothballs — what is it?
Naphthalene: Chemical compound. It is a white crystalline solid with a characteristic odor that is detectable at concentrations as low as 0.08 ppm.
Unlike its more predictably spreading cousin, this group of blood cancers can appear in multiple parts of the body at once and cause enlarged lymph nodes, fevers, and night sweats — which condition?
Non-Hodgkin lymphoma: Type of cancer of lymph nodes.

Found above 3,500 metres on the Tibetan Plateau, this parasitic fungus grows out of moth larvae and is prized — despite containing arsenic — as an aphrodisiac in traditional Chinese medicine. What is it commonly called?
Ophiocordyceps sinensis: Species of fungus. It parasitizes larvae of ghost moths and produces a fruiting body which is valued in traditional Chinese medicine and Nepalese medicine as an aphrodisiac.
From a single western-Mediterranean flowering plant come both a notorious drug and the tiny dark seeds sprinkled on your bagel — which species is it?
Papaver somniferum: Species of flowering plant in the poppy family.
Known for its speed, this large crow-sized raptor has a blue-grey back, barred white underparts, and a black head — an avivore with marked sexual dimorphism — what is it?
Peregrine falcon: Fastest known animal and common bird of prey.
Named after the Latin word for the magpie, a bird known for its opportunistic feeding habits, this eating disorder involves craving non-food objects — what is it?
Pica (disorder): Compulsive eating of non-food items.
Nicknamed the 'terror of Bengal' for choking waterways across the world, this South American aquatic plant is commonly known as water hyacinth — what is its scientific name?
Pontederia crassipes: Aquatic plant native to the Amazon basin.

Marketed under brand names like Sudafed, this nasal decongestant can act as a stimulant and appetite suppressant at higher doses, making it both a medicine-cabinet staple and, at times, a drug of abuse. What is it?
Pseudoephedrine: Synthetic decongestant. Pseudoephedrine is a sympathomimetic medication which is used as a nasal decongestant to treat nasal congestion.
Nicknamed the 'stinking corpse lily,' this Southeast Asian plant genus produces the world's largest flower and was first seen by a Briton in 1818 after a local servant pointed it out — which genus?
This plant genus includes redcurrants, blackcurrants, and gooseberries, and also serves as the main alternate host for a fungal disease that attacks five-needle pines — which genus?
Ribes: Genus of flowering plants in the order Saxifragales.

Also called cot or crib death, this leading cause of infant mortality in the West strikes a baby under one, usually while sleeping between midnight and 9 a.m., and stays unexplained even after a full autopsy. What is it?
SIDS: Sudden unexplained death of a child who is less than one year of age.

Named after a colourful terrestrial flower, this predatory marine cnidarian is typically a single polyp anchored to a hard surface — a tentacled relative of coral and jellyfish, but with no medusa stage. What is it?
Sea anemone: Marine animals of the order Actiniaria.
Sitting just below carbon in group 14 of the periodic table, this blue-grey, brittle semiconductor is essential to plants and dominates the world's transistors and solar cells — which element is it?
Silicon: Chemical element with atomic number 14 (Si)
Commonly grown as an easy-care houseplant that tolerates low light, this genus of about 60 tropical species is better known by the nickname 'peace lily' — what genus is it?
Spathiphyllum: Genus of plants. Certain species of Spathiphyllum are commonly known as spath or peace lilies.
Usually found in pairs and recognized as a leading cause of pneumonia since the late 19th century, which bacterium often lives harmlessly in the respiratory tracts of healthy carriers?
Streptococcus pneumoniae: Species of bacterium. Streptococcus pneumoniae, or pneumococcus, is a Gram-positive, spherical bacteria, alpha-hemolytic member of the genus Streptococcus.
Marketed under the brand name Flomax, this alpha-blocker medication treats enlarged prostate symptoms and helps ease the passage of kidney stones — which drug?
Tamsulosin: Medication. Tamsulosin, sold under the brand name Flomax among others, is a medication used to treat symptomatic benign prostatic hyperplasia and chronic prostatitis.
First unearthed in Mongolia's Gobi Desert in 1948, this Late Cretaceous giant is known mainly from claw bones over half a meter long, giving it a name meaning 'scythe lizard' — which dinosaur genus?
Therizinosaurus: Therizinosaurid genus from the Late Cretaceous period.

Famous for oversized, colorful bills nearly useless for excavation, these Neotropical birds nest in hollows dug by other animals and share an ecological niche with Africa and Asia's hornbills — what are they?
Toucan: Family of birds. The family includes five genera and over 40 different species.
Made from strained yogurt mixed with cucumber, garlic, and herbs like dill or mint, this cold Greek dip is a classic topping for souvlaki and gyros — what is it called?
Tzatziki: Cold cucumber–yogurt dip, soup, or sauce.

First glimpsed through Dmitri Ivanovsky's 1892 study of an ailing tobacco plant, this is the most numerous biological entity on Earth — yet it can only replicate inside another organism's living cells. What is it?
Virus: Infectious agent that replicates in cells.
This American child prodigy entered Harvard at 11 and lectured on four-dimensional geometry at 12 before deliberately retreating from public life — who was he?
William James Sidis: American mathematician, polyglot, and child prodigy (1898–1944)
Iron is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for iron is Fe. Iron is a chemical element; it has symbol Fe and atomic number 26.
Plutonium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for plutonium is Pu. Plutonium is a chemical element; it has symbol Pu and atomic number 94.
